stress_test.limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.

authored_scope: Supported: widths 5..30 sampled (3..30 explicit) and heights mostly 4..16 with occasional synthetic extension to 30. Sizes beyond the fixture range are synthetic extensions. Ground is a skyline in five styles (flat with an optional hole, random skyline, pillar frame, alternating stubs, pocket), optionally two-coloured per column. There are 1..8 movers: polyominoes, bars, rings, combs, lattices and bridged composites, with shape caps growing on large grids. No-gap stacking is enforced in about 40% of multi-object defaults. Explicit latent reconstruction is available through heights/ground_colors/movers. Deliberately not supported: ground with overhangs or floating ground, inputs where objects already touch each other or the ground, interleaved objects sharing columns with overlapping row ranges, and multicolour movers.
authored_constraints: Every ground cell lies in a column filled contiguously from the bottom row, so reference static detection agrees with the latent ground.
Movers are single-colour, 4-connected, at rows 0..h-2, and 8-separated from ground and from each other.
Movers sharing any column have disjoint row ranges, so the lowest-first order is a valid topological order and tie-breaks cannot change the output.
Mover colours differ from air and from every visible ground colour.
At least one mover shifts down by at least 1 row (no identity pairs).
Random skylines must contain a column with height <= h-3 whose neighbours have height <= h-2. This is necessary for any fall; explicit infeasible skylines are rejected early.
num_objects must not exceed ceil(w/2)*floor(h/2), the 8-separation capacity.
Booleans and non-int values are rejected for sizes, heights, colours, counts and coordinates.
All loops are bounded (400 scene attempts x 40 shape draws, then 60 fallback attempts, then ValueError).

diversity_audit.method: Bottom-contiguous ground and separate rigid objects; calculate maximal displacement from obstacle distances, without generator latent states or step simulation

original_audit.rule: Air is 7. Ground is every column filled up from the bottom edge (a per-column height of 0 or more; full-height columns are pillars). Every other single-colour 4-connected object falls straight down as a rigid body, lowest bottom row first. A falling cell may not enter the bottom row, so the grid edge acts as a virtual floor at row H. It may not overlap ground or an already-fallen object. It may not stop directly above a ground cell in its own column, so one empty row is left above ground. It may rest directly on an already-fallen object with no gap. Objects that cannot move stay where they are.

findings.location: _drop: stop test `(nr + 1, c) in static` (checks the cell's own column only)
findings.issue: In every canonical pair, each fallen object ends with no ground cell beside or diagonal to it. Two rules fit all five fixtures equally well: (a) the code's rule, where the gap is checked only in the cell's own column, and (b) 'stop before any cell becomes 8-adjacent to ground'. I traced the ring and tee in pair 3, the 9 in pair 4, and both test shapes, and all give the same result under (a) and (b). The generator settles on (a) and can produce scenes where they differ. For example, an object slides down beside a pillar or pocket wall and ends flush against it. Under (b), the same object would not move at all. Generated pairs therefore teach a behaviour the fixtures never show.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask the host to decide whether lateral contact with ground after falling is intended. If it is, keep it and document it as a synthetic extension. If it is not, reject sampled scenes where any fallen cell ends up 4-adjacent (or 8-adjacent) to ground in a column other than its own.
findings.test: generate(width=5, height=6, heights=[4,0,0,0,4], ground_colors=5, movers=[[3, [[0, 1]]]]) should succeed with output[4][1] == 3 next to output[4][0] == 5. Also count, over about 200 default samples, how often a fallen cell is horizontally adjacent to ground.

findings.location: generate: explicit-movers branch (`movers` length not compared with MAX_OBJECTS)
findings.issue: num_objects is limited to 1..8, but an explicit `movers` list of any length is accepted when num_objects is None. The object-count contract is therefore inconsistent across the two control paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject `len(movers) > MAX_OBJECTS`, or document that explicit scenes are exempt from the limit.
findings.test: generate(width=30, height=10, heights=[1]*30, ground_colors=5, movers=[[3, [[0, 2*k]]] for k in range(9)]) is currently accepted.

findings.location: generate: explicit `heights` path (no `sum(heights) == 0` check, unlike the sampled path in the random loop)
findings.issue: Explicit all-zero heights are accepted in both random and explicit-mover mode. The result is a scene with no visible ground at all. The sampled path rejects this case (`sum(hts) == 0`), and the reference explanation says every grid has solid ground.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reject explicit heights with no visible ground cell, or state in the docstring that ground-free scenes are an allowed extension.
findings.test: generate(heights=[0,0,0,0,0], ground_colors=3) currently succeeds, and its input contains only 7 and mover colours.

findings.location: _fallback: candidate sort `(p[0], fallable, key)` with single-cell movers
findings.issue: The fallback scene always uses 1x1 movers placed greedily from the top rows down, and it never tries for stacking. Tight but feasible controls (narrow grids, many objects, small heights) send generation to this path. Those scenes all follow a fixed template with very little shape or position diversity.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the fallback place small bars or dominoes as well as single cells, and randomise the row order. Alternatively, log or count fallback use so the host can see how often it happens.
findings.test: generate(width=3, num_objects=8) over 5 trials: check whether every mover is a single cell sitting in rows 0,2,4,...

findings.location: _place_objects inner loop (no early exit when an object fails 40 tries); _blob `random.choice(sorted(cells))`
findings.issue: When one object cannot be placed, the loop keeps trying to place all the remaining targets anyway, and the attempt is then thrown away (`len(placed) != target`). For infeasible explicit controls, the cost is roughly 400 x target x 40 shape draws plus 60 fallback rounds before ValueError. This is probably acceptable, but rejection latency has not been measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Return early from _place_objects as soon as one target fails all 40 tries. Use random.choice on a list kept alongside the set instead of sorting every iteration.
findings.test: Time generate(heights=[1,0,1], height=3, num_objects=2). It should raise ValueError, preferably in well under 1 s.

findings.location: _can_place: disjoint row ranges required for objects sharing a column
findings.issue: Objects that share a column must lie entirely above or below each other, and all objects are 8-separated. This makes the 'lowest first' ordering consistent, but it also means the order is never actually observable or stressed. Nested or interlocking layouts (for example, a cell under a comb's arms) never appear. This is a sound guard against ambiguity and also a known limit on diversity.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. Document this as an intentional exclusion.
findings.test: Invariant: for every pair of input movers that share a column, max_row(A) < min_row(B) or max_row(B) < min_row(A).

findings.location: _random_ground_colors (two-colour ground: tallest columns get colour a, others get b)
findings.issue: Multi-colour ground does not appear in any fixture. It is labelled as a synthetic extension. Every coloured column still touches the bottom row, so reading 'ground = touches bottom edge' still works.
findings.test: Invariant: in two-colour scenes, every non-7 cell whose colour is a ground colour sits in a column whose run of ground reaches row H-1.

targeted_checks: validate() should reproduce all 4 train pairs and the test pair exactly. I traced _drop by hand: pair 1 shifts are 1/1/2, pair 2 is 0/1, pair 3 is tee 1 and ring 4, pair 4 is 2, and the test is left 1 and right 2. Execution is still needed to confirm that common.grid(width, height, AIR) uses this argument order.
For every generated pair, run the reference transform on the input and compare it with the output (stable sort ties do not matter because tied objects never share a column).
Invariant: in columns of height 0, no output cell in row H-1 is non-air, and no input mover touches row H-1.
Invariant: input movers are 8-separated from each other and from ground, mover colours are not visible ground colours, and input != output.
Measure the stacking rate: about 40% of default calls should have _has_contact true.
Measure how often fallen objects end up laterally adjacent to ground (wall sliding) and report it for the host to decide.
Measure how often the fallback is used and how fast rejections are under tight controls.
scope_limits: Nothing was executed; all traces were done by hand.
The reference transform contains a dead clause (`ny + 1 > H - 1` can never hold because `ny < H-1`). It does not affect the generator.
The intended ARC semantics for lateral wall contact cannot be determined from the fixtures.
